case.pattern_description: Threshold structuring on a compromised card: 4 online purchases ($481.66, $468.32, $485.41, $469.47) placed within about an hour, each kept just under $500, the level at which authorisation checks tighten. It affects cardholders whose card numbers are already compromised and matches five closed cases the bank confirmed but could not map to a known typology; the agent found it by scanning the card's window for clusters of same-band amounts.

sar.narrative: Customer C02265, holder of card C02265-K1, is the subject of this report. Between 2016-12-02 19:00 and 2016-12-02 19:30, 4 transaction(s) totalling $1,904.86 were made on the card online from device profile 'Windows | Windows 10 | chrome 64.0 | 1920x1080': $481.66 (3507563, 2016-12-02 19:00), $468.32 (3507591, 2016-12-02 19:08), $485.41 (3507626, 2016-12-02 19:20), $469.47 (3507670, 2016-12-02 19:30). Every amount sat just below $500 and the purchases were placed minutes apart, a pattern consistent with deliberately staying under an authorisation threshold. The activity is suspicious because: 4 online purchases within 30 minutes, each between $400 and $500 ($481.66, $468.32, $485.41, $469.47; total $1,904.86). It closely resembles earlier confirmed fraud cases CC-4124, CC-3841, CC-3907. The bank has recommended blocking and reissuing the card, placed linked cards under monitoring where applicable, and retains the transaction, device and investigation records as supporting documentation.
